one_line.text: An American investigative journalist who turns behavioural research and reported cases into practical frameworks about habits, productivity, and communication.

biography.text: Duhigg is a Yale and Harvard Business School graduate who worked in private equity and education ventures before becoming a full-time journalist in 2003. He reported for the Los Angeles Times and The New York Times, including from Iraq, and now writes for The New Yorker. He was part of the New York Times team awarded the 2013 Pulitzer Prize for explanatory reporting on Apple's global business practices.

background.text: His training combines history and business education with long-form reporting. The Power of Habit grew from his interest in military routines while reporting in Iraq and uses the methods of explanatory journalism: interviews, scenes, documents, expert interpretation, and extensive notes. His later books use the same story-and-research structure for productivity and conversation.

expertise.text: His strongest demonstrated expertise is investigating organisations, interviewing specialists, and making technical material memorable for a general reader. Awards and a substantial reporting record support that craft. He is not presented by his own, employer, or publisher biographies as a neuroscientist, psychologist, clinician, or behaviour-change trialist, so scientific authority belongs to the cited studies rather than to his credentials.

perspective_and_limits.text: Duhigg favours a clear model carried by vivid personal and corporate stories. That makes concepts accessible and exposes institutional systems, but selected success stories can imply a single cause, compress contested research, or make an illustrative case feel representative. His business background and journalistic method help him enter organisations; they do not establish intervention efficacy or a complete theory of behaviour.

selected_works.title: The Power of Habit
selected_works.relationship: His first book establishes his signature blend of behavioural science, reporting, organisational cases, and an applied framework.

selected_works.title: Smarter Faster Better
selected_works.relationship: Extends the method from automatic behaviour to eight ideas about motivation, teams, focus, goals, management, decisions, innovation, and data.

selected_works.title: Supercommunicators
selected_works.relationship: Applies the same story-and-science approach to practical, emotional, and identity conversations.
